chicken-rice.name: Chicken Rice

reasons.better-not: Roasted skin is harder to digest

chicken-rice.portionTip: Start with half portion if you're not very hungry
chicken-rice.sauceTip:
👍 Chilli — small amount
⚠️ Ginger — moderate
🚫 Dark soy / sweet sauce — high sugar & sodium

fish-soup.name: Fish Soup

options.better-not: Fried fish + evaporated milk in soup

reasons.safer: Pure protein and hydrating soup. Perfect if you’re feeling bloated or want a light meal.
reasons.sometimes: You get the crunch and richness of fried batter, but the clear soup keeps it from feeling like a "heavy" meal.
reasons.better-not: Saturated fat from the evaporated milk combined with the deep-fry oil from the fish batter. Common culprit for a massive energy crash.

fish-soup.portionTip:
The Noodle Strategy: If you want to feel "lighter," opt for Thick Bee Hoon or Rice. Thin Bee Hoon and Mee Sua act like sponges; they soak up significantly more sodium and oil from the broth compared to Thick Bee Hoon.

The "Side" Swap: Ask for extra Bitter Gourd or Silken Tofu. This adds volume and "mouthfeel" to the meal without the heaviness of double-fried fish.

The Egg Floss Trap: If the stall offers Fried Egg Floss (those golden crunchy bits), ask for it on the side or skip it. It's 90% oil and quickly turns a "safe" clear soup into a high-fat meal.

The 70% Rule: You don't need to finish the broth! Enjoy the fish and noodles, drink enough soup to feel satisfied, but leave the last bit in the bowl to avoid the heaviest concentration of salt.
fish-soup.sauceTip:
• Chili Padi + Soy Sauce
  Dip, don't pour. Dipping your fish gives you the salt hit without making the whole soup a sodium bomb.

• Minced Ginger
  Recommended. Great for "warming" the body and aiding digestion, with zero added fats.

• Fried Shallots/Garlic
  A sprinkle is fine. They add great aroma, but they are deep-fried.

yong-tau-foo.name: Yong Tau Foo

options.safer: Soup base with fresh tofu and greens
options.sometimes: Dry style with sweet bean sauce
options.better-not: Laksa broth or mostly crispy fried items

reasons.safer: Soft tofu is easy to digest
reasons.better-not: Fried items are harder to process

yong-tau-foo.portionTip: Fill up with more tofu and vegetables
yong-tau-foo.sauceTip:
👍 Clear soup — small
⚠️ Sweet sauce — moderate
🚫 Chill paste — can be spicy

ban-mian.name: Ban Mian

options.better-not: Dry style with extra chilli oil and fried ikan bilis

ban-mian.portionTip: Share noodles if portion looks large
ban-mian.sauceTip:
👍 Ketchup — small
⚠️ Chilli oil — moderate
🚫 Vinegar — high acidity

nasi-lemak.name: Nasi Lemak

options.safer: Plain rice with ikan bilis, egg, and cucumber
options.sometimes: Coconut rice with otah and wings
options.better-not: Coconut rice with extra sambal and fried sides

reasons.better-not: Fried sides and sambal are heavy

nasi-lemak.portionTip: Skip the fried chicken, have more cucumber
nasi-lemak.sauceTip:
👍 Light sambal — small
⚠️ Coconut milk — moderate
🚫 Extra sambal — high sugar & oil

wanton-mee.name: Wanton Mee

options.better-not: Dry version with extra sauce and fried wantons

reasons.better-not: Extra sauce and oil are heavy

wanton-mee.portionTip: Ask for fewer noodles, more veggies
wanton-mee.sauceTip:
👍 Soup — small
⚠️ Chilli powder — moderate
🚫 Extra sauce/oil — heavy

carrot-cake.name: Carrot Cake

options.safer: White version with more egg, less oil

reasons.safer: Egg adds protein without much oil

carrot-cake.portionTip: Share between two, it's quite filling
carrot-cake.sauceTip:
👍 White sauce — small
⚠️ Sweet sauce — moderate
🚫 Black sauce — high sugar

economical-rice.name: Economical Rice

options.safer: Two steamed vegetable sides + 1 steamed protein
options.better-not: Multiple fried sides or heavy gravy over rice

economical-rice.portionTip: Choose smaller rice portion, more veg
economical-rice.sauceTip:
👍 Light gravy — small
⚠️ Oyster sauce — moderate
🚫 Heavy curry/gravy — high oil

laksa.name: Laksa

options.better-not: Extra soup or added fried toppings

laksa.portionTip: Have half the noodles, more bean sprouts
laksa.sauceTip:
👍 Lime — small
⚠️ Sambal — moderate
🚫 Extra coconut milk — very rich

bak-chor-mee.name: Bak Chor Mee

options.safer: Soup version with minced meat and mushrooms

bak-chor-mee.portionTip: Ask for less mee (noodles), add more mushrooms
bak-chor-mee.sauceTip:
👍 Soup — small
⚠️ Vinegar — moderate
🚫 Chilli/lard — heavy

vision.title: The Vision
vision.content: Eating in Singapore is a national pastime, but it can often feel like a source of stress or "health guilt." Eat Outside was created to help you navigate our beautiful food centres with more ease and less anxiety.

philosophy.title: Our Philosophy
philosophy.content: , not restriction. You don't need to stop eating the foods you love to feel better. We don't use calorie counts or clinical language. Instead, we offer simple adjustments that make your favourite meals feel a little lighter on the palate.

howTo.title: How to Use This
howTo.content: Think of this as a gentle friend sitting across the table. Pick your dish and see the options. Whether you choose a Light, Caution, or Avoid version depends entirely on how you feel today—there are no wrong answers.

notMedical.title: Not Medical Advice
notMedical.content: The information provided is for educational and supportive purposes only. We are not medical professionals. Suggestions are based on common preparation methods and general body-feel.

listenBody.title: Listen to Your Body
listenBody.content: Every body is different. Please prioritise your own comfort, medical requirements, and the advice of your healthcare provider.

allergies.title: Allergies & Safety
allergies.content: Always check with hawker stall owners regarding ingredients and allergens. Recipes can change without notice.
